text.p: These are the leading stories in the Mozambican press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mozambique's parliament continued debating the government's new land law on Thursday, with the opposition Renamo party demanding that hereditary chiefs have a say in the allocation of title deeds. The government did not include the chiefs in the bill because, it says, the traditional system discrminates against women.

- Training courses begin on Monday for the people who will carry out Mozambique's national census in the first fortnight in August. There will be 30,000 census agents and 1,000 controllers. The agents have to learn how to fill in a 68-question form in half an hour, so that they can cover 10 families a day in towns and eight in rural areas.
